title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
prompt:
Evaluate an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish (postfix) Notation. `tokens` is `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, or integers. Division truncates toward zero.

**Example**: `["2","1","+","3","*"]` → `9` (i.e. `(2+1)*3`).

A stack: push numbers; on an operator, pop two operands, combine, push the result.

tests.note: order: a - b where b was popped first

hints: Push each integer. On an operator, pop `b` then `a` (order matters for - and /).
The result is `a op b` — pushed back for later operators to consume.
`Integer.parseInt` handles negative tokens like "-11"; distinguish them from the "-" operator by checking the operator cases first.

solution.explanation: O(n). Postfix needs no parentheses because operand order is unambiguous — the two most recent results on the stack are exactly this operator's arguments. Popping `b` before `a` preserves left-to-right order for the non-commutative `-` and `/`.
